description: The body systems, how they fail, and the language clinicians use to describe them, taught for future health informaticians who must read and code clinical records. Students step through physiology processes, decode terms and notes, query lab results and work branching patient cases drawn from Ghanaian health practice.
modelledOn: Tortora and Derrickson, Principles of Anatomy and Physiology
World Health Organization, ICD-10 and ICD-11 classification and the Model List of Essential Medicines
Bickley, Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
outcomes: Describe the structure and function of the major body systems and explain how homeostasis is maintained.
Build, split and interpret medical terms from word roots, prefixes and suffixes, and decode common abbreviations safely.
Explain how common diseases in Ghana present, are diagnosed with procedures and laboratory tests, and are classified for coding.
Describe how common drug classes act and calculate simple weight-based doses and half-life effects.
Measure, record and interpret vital signs and clinical measurements, including units, reference ranges and early warning scores.
Read a clinical note and chart end to end and extract the problems, medications, results and plan.

units.title: Organisation of the body and the language of medicine
topics: Levels of organisation from cell to organism; homeostasis and negative and positive feedback
Anatomical position, body planes, directional terms and body cavities
Word roots, combining forms, prefixes and suffixes; building and splitting terms
Abbreviations, eponyms and error-prone shorthand; do-not-use lists
Spelling, pronunciation and plural forms of Greek and Latin terms

units.title: Cardiovascular, blood and respiratory systems
topics: Heart anatomy, the cardiac cycle, the conduction system and the electrocardiogram
Blood vessels, blood pressure regulation and circulation
Blood: cells, haemoglobin, clotting, blood groups and sickle cell disease
Airways, lungs, ventilation and gas exchange
Lung volumes, oxygen transport and acid-base balance
Common diseases: hypertension, heart failure, anaemia, asthma, pneumonia and tuberculosis

units.title: Digestive, renal, endocrine and reproductive systems
topics: Digestive tract and accessory organs; digestion and absorption
Liver function, metabolism and viral hepatitis
Kidney and nephron: filtration, fluid and electrolyte balance, urinary tract infection
Endocrine glands and hormones; insulin, glucose regulation and diabetes mellitus
Reproductive system, pregnancy, antenatal care and childbirth
Common diseases: peptic ulcer, cholera, typhoid, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disorders

units.title: Nervous, musculoskeletal, skin and immune systems
topics: Brain, spinal cord, neurons, action potentials and reflexes
Special senses: eye, ear, taste and smell
Bones, joints and muscles; fractures and their healing
Skin structure, wound healing and burns
Immune system: innate and adaptive immunity, vaccines and HIV infection
Common diseases: stroke, epilepsy, meningitis, osteoporosis and skin infections

units.title: Diseases, diagnoses, procedures and laboratory tests
topics: Disease processes: infection, inflammation, neoplasia and degeneration; malaria, tuberculosis, HIV and non-communicable diseases in Ghana
Symptoms, signs and syndromes; history taking and differential diagnosis
Diagnosis classification and coding with ICD-10, ICD-11 and SNOMED CT concepts
Imaging and procedures: X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI and endoscopy; procedure coding
Laboratory tests: full blood count, malaria rapid test, glucose, liver and kidney panels, urinalysis; reference ranges and LOINC

units.title: Medications and pharmacology basics
topics: Drug names, classes and the essential medicines list; generic versus brand
Pharmacokinetics: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and half-life
Pharmacodynamics: receptors, dose-response curves and the therapeutic index
Routes, dosage forms, weight-based dose calculation and prescription abbreviations
Adverse reactions, interactions, allergies, counterfeit medicines and pharmacovigilance

units.title: Vital signs and clinical measurements
topics: Temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, blood pressure and oxygen saturation
Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, growth charts and mid-upper arm circumference
Early warning scores and triage categories
Units, reference ranges and conversions such as mg/dL and mmol/L; device error and data quality
Consciousness and pain: Glasgow coma scale and pain scales

units.title: Reading a clinical note and chart
topics: SOAP note structure: history, examination, assessment and plan
Medication charts, orders and administration records
Referral letters, discharge summaries and the problem list
Decoding a complete chart end to end, with confidentiality of patient records

schedule.title: Levels of organisation and anatomical language
schedule.exercise: Label the planes, directional terms and body cavities on a diagram, and trace a feedback loop for body temperature with sensor, control centre and effector.

tasks.title: Describe the location of six injuries to a triage nurse using correct directional terms and planes, and score each description for precision
Step through a negative feedback loop for blood glucose, change the set point and disturbance, and record how the response variable returns to normal
Plot body temperature against time with a faulty sensor and a positive feedback loop, and compare how each loop reacts to the same disturbance

schedule.title: Building and decoding medical terms
schedule.exercise: Split twenty terms into prefix, root and suffix, build five new terms from definitions, and rewrite ten ambiguous abbreviations in full.

tasks.title: Query a table of 200 word parts to split twenty clinical terms into prefix, root and suffix, then give the meaning of each term
Review 12 handwritten orders for dangerous abbreviations, rewrite each safely, and be scored on the harm avoided in the branching ward case
Write a small program that splits a medical term using a word-part dictionary, then test it on 30 terms and list the ones it gets wrong

schedule.title: Heart, vessels and blood
schedule.exercise: Draw the path of blood through the heart, annotate one cardiac cycle on an ECG trace, and match blood groups for four transfusion pairs.

tasks.title: Step through the cardiac cycle and conduction pathway, and mark where each ECG wave P, QRS and T appears in the sequence
Plot blood pressure against changing heart rate and vessel resistance with a simple model, and identify which change raises mean arterial pressure most
Cross-match four transfusion cases for ABO and Rhesus groups, release or refuse each unit, and justify the choice against the safety rubric

schedule.title: Breathing, gas exchange and common conditions
schedule.exercise: Explain how an asthma attack changes airflow and gas exchange, and interpret one arterial blood gas for acidosis or alkalosis.

tasks.title: Step through inhalation and exhalation, changing lung compliance and airway resistance, and note how tidal volume and oxygen exchange respond
Plot the oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve, shift it for acidity and temperature, and read oxygen saturation at three given partial pressures
Assess a child with cough, fever and fast breathing in a case, decide between pneumonia, asthma and tuberculosis, and be scored on safe referral

schedule.title: Digestion, liver and kidney
schedule.exercise: Follow a meal from mouth to absorption, explain what hepatitis B does to liver function tests, and calculate net filtration pressure in the glomerulus.

tasks.title: Step through digestion of a meal of fufu and soup, recording the organ, enzyme and product at each stage of absorption
Query liver function results for 40 patients, list those with raised bilirubin and transaminases, and group the pattern by likely cause
Step through filtration, reabsorption and secretion in the nephron, then change the blood pressure and fluid intake and note how urine volume responds

schedule.title: Hormones, reproduction and gut infections
schedule.exercise: Contrast type 1 and type 2 diabetes with insulin action, list antenatal visits and their checks, and describe how cholera causes dehydration.

tasks.title: Plot blood glucose over 24 hours for a healthy person and a person with diabetes after meals, and find where insulin action fails
Run an antenatal clinic case: schedule visits, interpret blood pressure and haemoglobin results, and spot the pre-eclampsia warning signs in time
Manage a cholera outbreak case in a market town: triage patients, start rehydration and report cases, and be scored on lives saved and spread contained

schedule.title: Nervous system, senses and the skeleton
schedule.exercise: Draw the pathway of a reflex arc, describe how the eye forms an image, and classify four fractures with their treatment.

tasks.title: Step through a neuron action potential, changing the stimulus strength, and record threshold, depolarisation, repolarisation and the all-or-none response
Examine a patient with sudden weakness on one side, choose the right neurological checks, and decide whether the findings fit a stroke
Query a trauma register to count fractures by bone and age band, and identify the groups where osteoporosis is the most likely cause

schedule.title: Skin, immunity and related diseases
schedule.exercise: Compare innate and adaptive immune responses, explain how a vaccine works, and describe the course of untreated HIV infection.

tasks.title: Step through an immune response to a first and second exposure of the same antigen and compare antibody levels and speed
Plot CD4 count and viral load over ten years for a patient with and without treatment, and mark when opportunistic infection risk rises
Work up a patient with fever, neck stiffness and headache in a case, order the right tests and treatment, and be scored on speed to treatment

schedule.title: Disease, diagnosis, procedures and tests
schedule.exercise: Take a history for fever and rash, list a differential diagnosis, assign ICD codes, and interpret a full blood count and malaria test.

tasks.title: Query a laboratory table for haemoglobin and white cell results, flag values outside reference ranges, and count abnormal results by ward
Map 20 diagnoses written in free text to ICD-10 codes in a lookup table, and list the ones that need a more specific code
Work up a patient with fever through history, examination, imaging and lab tests, narrow the differential, and be scored on tests chosen versus cost

schedule.title: Drug names, kinetics and dynamics
schedule.exercise: Group ten medicines into classes using the essential medicines list, and sketch the plasma concentration curve for an oral dose.

tasks.title: Search an essential medicines table by class to find generic names for five brand-name drugs and list their routes and dose forms
Plot plasma concentration over 24 hours for repeated doses with a given half-life, and find when steady state is reached
Plot dose-response curves for two drugs, read the median effective dose of each, and compare their therapeutic index from the curves

schedule.title: Dosing, safety and adverse effects
schedule.exercise: Calculate a weight-based paracetamol dose for a child, decode five prescription abbreviations, and report an adverse reaction to a pharmacovigilance form.

tasks.title: Write a small program that computes weight-based doses for ten children from mg per kg and flags any dose above the maximum
Review a patient's medication list in a case, find a dangerous interaction and an allergy conflict, and change the prescription safely
Investigate a batch of suspected counterfeit antimalarials in a district case: trace the supply, report to the regulator and protect patients

schedule.title: Vital signs and measurements
schedule.exercise: Record vital signs for four patients, compute BMI and early warning scores, and convert glucose and creatinine values between unit systems.

tasks.title: Measure and record vital signs for four simulated patients on a ward round, spot the one deteriorating, and escalate at the right time
Code an early warning score from respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, pulse, blood pressure and consciousness, and test it on 20 patient observations
Convert 15 glucose, cholesterol and creatinine results between mg/dL and mmol/L, then plot growth for a child on a standard chart

schedule.title: Reading a clinical note and chart
schedule.exercise: Read a complete record for a patient with diabetes and hypertension and write a one-paragraph summary with problems, medicines, results and plan.

tasks.title: Read a SOAP note and highlight the subjective, objective, assessment and plan statements, scoring each correct classification
Query medication orders and administration records for ward patients to find doses ordered but not given and drugs given without an order
Review an entire chart in a case, extract the problem list and key results, decode all abbreviations, and brief the next shift without missing a risk
